newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Sahara ceremony for Algerian gas line to Europe.
newsitem.headline: Sahara ceremony for Algerian gas line to Europe.

text.p: Less than 30 months after the first trench was carved out for a 1,385 km (865 mile) gas pipeline, energy ministers of Algeria, Morocco, Spain and Portugal on Saturday attend a ceremony to open the taps.

The official inauguration sets the seal on an investment of some $2.0 billion for the line capable of carrying 9.5 billion cubic metres of gas from Algeria's Sahara Desert field of Hassi R'mel to Spain and Portugal.
"This pipeline puts us in a good position for the European market," said Nazim Zouioueche, director-general of Algeria's state oil and gas firm, Sonatrach, this week.

Besides the immediate Iberian peninsula market, Morocco will later benefit from gas deliveries and, with the possibility of pipeline capacity being lifted to 18 billion cubic metres annually around the year 2,000, France and Germany are also potential markets.

The Maghreb gas pipeline, on which a first agreement was signed in 1991, runs from the gas field, across Morocco, under the Strait of Gibraltar, to the Spanish city of Cordoba, and is to link up with a gas distribution network for Portugal.

Zouioueche termed pipeline distribution a particularly "attractive link" on a regional basis, recalling that Algeria had another pipeline from Hassi R'mel to Italy, via Tunisia. This went into service in 1982.
"We are satisfied with this sharing in the two means of exporting our gas" towards Europe, he told the official Algerian news agency APS.
APS said that by the year 2,000, Algerian gas would cover 12 percent of Spain's energy consumption.

Natural gas has actually started flowing in the pipeline already, with APS reporting from Madrid that, after technical trials, the first constant flow arrived at Zahara de los Atunes, near Cadiz, on November 1.
Algeria hopes to double its present annual gas exports to 60 billion cubic metres by the year 2,000, when one Algerian official said its oil and gas exports should earn $16 billion.
Morocco will use gas from Hassi R'mel, including for electricity generation, when it has set up the infrastructure. Until then it will take a share of the income generated.
To the south of Hassi R'mel, another project is already under way. Britain's BP has a $3 billion deal with Sonatrach for gas exploration and development in the inhospitable desert.
If successful, another pipeline -- of around 500 km (310 miles) -- may be needed to carry more gas to Hassi R'mel and then onto Europe.
